## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), Theorem 5.4 states that \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) is generated by each of the two indicated Schur intervals; each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [source-backed] The original paper labels minimality of these generating sets a conjecture and reports computation only for \(r\le4\) and \(q=n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1489-1502]
- [proved] Assume the integral box-Schur/Pieri presentation: \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) is connected graded with integral Schur bases, truncated Pieri holds, and \(\Lambda_+J_v=A_+J_v\). If \(a=1,b=2\), then
  \[
  J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2,
  \]
  where
  \[
  x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad
  x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}.
  \]
  Consequently both Theorem 5.4 families
  \[
  (x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad
  (x_0,y_1,y_2),\quad
  y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\ y_2=s_{(i^j,2)},
  \]
  map to integral bases and are minimal generating sets.

## Strategy
Put \(\alpha=q-i\), \(\beta=r-j\). The hypotheses \(a=1,b=2\) imply
\[
i,j,\alpha,\beta\ge1,\qquad \min(i,j)=2,\qquad \min(\alpha,\beta)=1.
\]
Thus \(x_0,x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2\) are inside the \(q^r\)-box. Let \(d=ij\).

The first family generates \(J_v\), so \(Q:=J_v/A_+J_v\) is generated over \(\mathbb Z\) by \(\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\bar x_2\), in degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\). Hence it suffices to prove that each is primitive and nonzero in its own degree.

In degree \(d+1\), truncated Pieri gives
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1.
\]
Use this as the unit pivot eliminating \(y_1\); the quotient is freely generated by \(\bar x_1\), and \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\).

In degree \(d+2\), define
\[
u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})},\quad
z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\quad
w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}.
\]
Here \(u\) is absent exactly when \(\alpha=1\), and \(w\) is absent exactly when \(\beta=1\). Pieri gives
\[
R:=h_1x_1=u+x_2+z,\qquad
P:=h_2x_0=u+z+y_2,\qquad
T:=h_1y_1=z+y_2+w,
\]
with outside-box terms omitted. Since
\[
(A_+J_v)_{d+2}=\mathbb ZP+\mathbb ZR+\mathbb ZT,
\]
these rows give a unit-pivot, degree-compatible elimination:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{case}&\text{unit-pivot order}&\text{survivor}\\ \hline
\alpha=1,\ \beta>1&z\text{ via }R,\ y_2\text{ via }P,\ w\text{ via }T&x_2\\
\alpha=1,\ \beta=1&z\text{ via }R,\ y_2\text{ via }P,\ T\mapsto0&x_2\\
\beta=1,\ \alpha>1&z\text{ via }R,\ y_2\text{ via }P,\ u\text{ via }T&x_2
\end{array}
\]

All pivots have coefficient \(1\). After the listed eliminations, no residual row involves \(x_2\). Thus the relation lattice is saturated and the degree-\(d+2\) quotient is \(\mathbb Z\bar x_2\), with no torsion.

Moreover,
\[
R-P=x_2-y_2\quad\text{in }Q,
\]
so \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\). Hence the two proposed families differ in \(Q\) by
\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1),
\]
an integral unimodular matrix. The source’s graded generating criterion then gives minimality. [source-2, lines 1520-1540]

## Gaps
- The proof is conditional on the integral box-Schur basis and truncated-Pieri presentation; the supplied primary excerpt states ideal generation but does not itself supply that presentation.
- This is a degreewise elimination, not an independent global Schur-column elimination of every degree. Such a global elimination is unnecessary once Theorem 5.4 generation is used to show that \(Q\) is generated in degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\).
